summary: Hostile audit #15 — the integration assembly script (setup/unload/reload/flow)

survived.title: Panels registered outside async_setup_entry are never tracked, so unload can't remove them and setup silently re-adds the "no vacuum configured" fallback panel
survived.mechanism: async_setup_entry tracks panels ONLY by what its own loop registers: `panel_url = await async_register_vacuum_panel(...)` / `if panel_url: registered_panels.append(panel_url)` (415-421), stored at 450 as hass.data[DOMAIN][f"_panels_{entry.entry_id}"], and async_unload_entry (471-478) removes exactly that list. `async_register_vacuum_panel` (panels.py:80-89) returns None when the url is already registered — HA's frontend.async_register_built_in_panel raises ValueError on a duplicate (verified in installed HA 2026.5, frontend/__init__.py:387-388) and panels.py swallows it at DEBUG. A grep proves nothing else ever appends to `_panels_<entry_id>`, yet setup/workflow.py:106 (add_vacuum, reached from the panel's own onboarding service) registers a per-vacuum panel outside setup. services/setup.py:161-167 then schedules a config-entry reload immediately after a successful add, so the bad interleaving is automatic, not hypothetical: (1) add_vacuum registers `eufy-vacuum-<obj>` untracked; (2) the auto-reload's unload pops the tracked list — which holds only the fallback `eufy-vacuum` — and leaves `eufy-vacuum-<obj>` registered in hass.data[DATA_PANELS]; (3) the new setup's loop hits ValueError for that vacuum, gets None, so `registered_panels` stays empty and the vacuum's panel remains untracked forever; (4) because `registered_panels` is empty the `if not registered_panels:` branch (428) fires and re-registers the fallback setup-placeholder panel. The state is self-perpetuating across every subsequent reload because step 3 repeats; only a full HA restart (which clears the in-memory panel dict) resets it. Note also that the re-used registration keeps the OLD `js_url` mtime cache-buster from _frontend_url.py, so the documented "a config entry reload re-registers the panel so browsers pick up a new bundle" contract silently does not hold for these vacuums.
survived.user_impact: Right after onboarding a vacuum through the panel (the documented primary path — the config flow's vacuum field is optional and the default notes text tells the user to add the vacuum from the sidebar panel), the sidebar shows a duplicate "Vacuum Agent" entry that renders the "no vacuum configured, go to Settings -> Configure" placeholder, and it comes back on every reload. The real vacuum panel is never removed when the integration is unloaded, disabled or deleted, so it lingers in the sidebar pointing at a dead backend until HA is restarted. Every second and later vacuum is affected unconditionally, since the config entry can carry only one vacuum_entity_id and all others must be added through add_vacuum. No error is shown — the duplicate-registration ValueError is logged at DEBUG.
survived.guards_checked: panels.py:79-89 (ValueError caught, returns None — the only signal, and the caller treats None as "nothing to track"); the `if panel_url:` guard at 420 (it is what drops the url); the fallback-panel try/except ValueError at 447-448 (catches its own duplicate, does not repair the list); _remove_panel_for_vacuum (562-573) and _teardown_vacuum (624) — they do remove an untracked panel, but only on device deletion, not on unload; grep for `_panels_` across the repo — only __init__.py touches it, so setup/workflow.py:106 and services/setup.py:307 (rename, replace=True) never register their urls; services/setup.py:161-167 confirms the reload that triggers the interleaving; tests/integration/test_init_setup.py:66-70 patches panel_custom.async_register_panel with an AsyncMock that never raises ValueError, so no test covers this path.
confirmations: CONFIRMED from source. Verified each link: (1) HA frontend/__init__.py async_register_built_in_panel raises ValueError("Overwriting panel ...") when frontend_url_path is already in hass.data[DATA_PANELS] and update=False; panel_custom.async_register_panel calls it WITHOUT update=, so the default False applies. (2) panels.py:89-91 catches that ValueError and returns None. (3) __init__.py:420 `if panel_url:` drops the None, so nothing is appended. (4) grep -rn '_panels_' across the package returns exactly 4 hits, all in __init__.py (450 write, 471 pop, 569/572 the _remove_panel_for_vacuum scan) — setup/workflow.py:104-110 (add_vacuum) registers a per-vacuum panel and appends to nothing. (5) services/setup.py setup_add_vacuum does `hass.async_create_task(hass.config_entries.async_reload(entries[0].entry_id))` on a success result, so the reload is automatic, not hypothetical. (6) I walked the single-vacuum steady state: unload pops ['eufy-vacuum'] (the fallback, the only tracked url) and removes it; the untracked 'eufy-vacuum-<obj>' survives in DATA_PANELS; the new setup's loop gets None for it, so registered_panels==[] and the `if not registered_panels:` branch at 428 re-registers the fallback placeholder. This repeats on every reload — self-perpetuating until an HA restart clears the in-memory panel dict. Confirmed the test blind spot too: tests/integration/test_init_setup.py _patch_frontend() patches homeassistant.components.panel_custom.async_register_panel with an AsyncMock, so the duplicate-url ValueError never fires under test. Minor overreach that does not change the verdict: services/setup.py:307 (setup_set_panel_title) uses replace=True on the SAME url, which is already in the tracked list, so that call site is harmless — workflow.py:106 is the only untracked registrar.

MECHANISM VERIFIED, ONE SUB-CLAIM OVER-STATED, SEVERITY OVER-RATED.

Verified from source: __init__.py:412-421 builds `registered_panels` only from what its own loop registers; :450 stores it as `_panels_<entry_id>`; async_unload_entry:471 pops exactly that list. panels.py:89-91 swallows ValueError and returns None. HA 2026.5.3 confirmed: frontend/__init__.py:386-387 `if not update and panel.frontend_url_path in panels: raise ValueError(...)`, and panel_custom/__init__.py:123-131 calls async_register_built_in_panel WITHOUT `update=`, so it defaults False -> duplicate url raises. setup/workflow.py:105-110 registers a per-vacuum panel and appends nowhere; services/setup.py:161-167 schedules `hass.async_create_task(hass.config_entries.async_reload(...))` right after a successful add. grep confirms only __init__.py ever touches `_panels_`. Test claim confirmed: tests/integration/test_init_setup.py:65-70 patches panel_custom.async_register_panel with AsyncMock (never raises), and grep for `_panels_` across tests/ returns nothing.

CONCRETE REPRODUCER (I re-derived it and it only works from a BLANK install): install with the vacuum picker left blank (config_flow.py:62 makes it Optional and the default notes string at :64-67 literally instructs the user to add it from the sidebar panel) -> get_known_vacuum_ids() empty -> `registered_panels == []` -> fallback 'eufy-vacuum' registered AND tracked. User adds the vacuum from that panel -> workflow.add_vacuum registers 'eufy-vacuum-<obj>' untracked -> services/setup.py auto-reload fires -> unload pops ['eufy-vacuum'] and removes only the fallback -> new setup registers 'eufy-vacuum-<obj>' -> already present -> ValueError -> None -> NOT appended -> `registered_panels` empty -> the `if not registered_panels:` branch at :428 re-registers the fallback placeholder. Steady state: TWO sidebar 'Vacuum Agent' entries, one rendering 'no vacuum configured'. Repeats on every reload; only a full HA restart clears hass.data[DATA_PANELS].

CORRECTION to the mechanism text: the claim 'every second and later vacuum is affected unconditionally' by the FALLBACK symptom is wrong. With vacuum A already tracked and B added via the panel, unload removes A, setup re-registers A successfully, `registered_panels` is NON-empty, and the fallback branch does not fire. For 2+ vacuums the only symptom is B's panel being permanently untracked (survives unload/disable/delete until restart) — which is exactly what A4-RELOAD-1 claims. The duplicate-fallback loop is specific to the all-vacuums-untracked case, i.e. the first vacuum added via the panel.

SEVERITY: not HIGH. Nothing durable is destroyed, the robot is unaffected, and an HA restart fully self-heals it. It is a persistent, unexplained sidebar-presentation defect on the documented onboarding path -> MEDIUM. (The `js_url` cache-buster sub-claim is also correct — the stale registration keeps its old `?v=` — but that is a cosmetic consequence, not independent severity.)

survived.title: async_setup_entry has no failure unwind, and HA never calls async_unload_entry for an entry that failed setup — a mid-setup raise orphans every subsystem registered so far and the next reload builds a second live copy
survived.mechanism: Setup registers roughly 20 long-lived things (see the inventory table) but attaches exactly ONE of them to the entry's unwind hook — `entry.async_on_unload(entry.add_update_listener(...))` at 265. There is no try/except or try/finally around the assembly, and only the per-vacuum loops (307-314, 327-333, 371-388) and the entity-registry cleanup (274-290) are individually guarded; `battery_manager.start()` (336), `error_tracker.start()` (344), the four `await async_register_*_services` calls (390-393) and the eight `*.register(hass)` calls (398-405) are unguarded. In installed HA 2026.5, an exception out of async_setup_entry is caught at config_entries.py:882-886, the state is set to SETUP_ERROR, and `_async_process_on_unload` runs only the entry.async_on_unload callbacks — our async_unload_entry is NOT called. Worse, a later reload also skips it: ConfigEntry.async_unload returns early at config_entries.py:1007-1010 whenever the state is not LOADED. So everything registered before the raise stays subscribed for the rest of the HA session, and the user's natural response (Reload) runs async_setup_entry again, producing a SECOND BatteryHealthManager, ErrorTracker, MappingTracker, manager and adapter coordinator while the first set's state listeners are still live. The first ErrorTracker's handlers write into the OLD manager's self.data and fire-and-forget `self._manager.async_save()` (core/error_tracker.py:1061-1070), which writes that stale blob over the store — the same clobber mechanism already verified as CRITICAL in audit #14, reached here by a different trigger. This is a cross-await gap, not a synchronous-block claim.
survived.user_impact: After any setup failure (a corrupt/hand-edited storage block reaching an unguarded ensure_record, an ImportError in a lazily-imported listener module after an update, an exception in any service registration), the integration is left half-built with no cleanup, and reloading — the obvious user action, and what the options flow does automatically — duplicates every state listener and timer. The duplicated old subsystems keep writing an increasingly stale copy of the whole storage blob over the live one, so room/job/learning edits made after the reload silently disappear. Nothing surfaces this beyond the single "Error setting up entry" traceback from the original failure.
survived.guards_checked: entry.async_on_unload at 265 — the only unwind hook, covers just the update listener; the per-vacuum try/except blocks at 307-314, 327-333, 371-388 and the registry-cleanup try/except at 274-290 — none of them wrap the registration steps themselves; the ConfigEntryNotReady at 237-240 — it is raised before anything but the coordinator exists, so the retry path itself is harmless and is NOT the concern; listeners/*.register() each call remove() first (verified in lifecycle.py:76, discovery.py:55, pause_timeout.py:52, pose_sampler.py:289, job_progress.py:55) so listener re-registration is idempotent — but BatteryHealthManager/ErrorTracker/MappingTracker/EufyVacuumManager are fresh INSTANCES whose per-instance idempotency guards (battery/manager.py:393, core/error_tracker.py:381) cannot see the previous instance's subscriptions; HA source verified at config_entries.py:882-886 and 1007-1010.
confirmations: CONFIRMED, including both HA claims which I read directly. config_entries.py: the broad `except SystemExit, Exception` around async_setup_entry logs 'Error setting up entry %s for %s' and the `finally:` runs only `await self._async_process_on_unload(hass)` — our async_unload_entry is never called. And ConfigEntry.async_unload early-returns True with `if self.state is not ConfigEntryState.LOADED:` after async_cancel_retry_setup, so a later user-triggered Reload also skips async_unload_entry. On our side I confirmed entry.async_on_unload appears EXACTLY ONCE in the whole entry setup (__init__.py:265, the update listener); battery_manager.start() (336), error_tracker.start() (344), the four service registrations (390-393), the eight listener register() calls (398-405) and async_forward_entry_setups (407) are all unguarded with no try/finally around the assembly. The stale-write consequence is real: core/error_tracker.py _persist_and_notify does `self._hass.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._hass.async_create_task, self._manager.async_save())` — an orphaned tracker holding the OLD manager writes that whole stale blob over the store, the audit #14 mechanism reached by a different trigger. Weakness I probed and am recording rather than refuting on: no concretely reachable raise is demonstrated (the two guarded hazards — manager init and ensure_vacuum_record — are both already wrapped), so the trigger is structural rather than proven. That is what keeps it MEDIUM and not higher; the ABSENCE of any unwind path is itself a genuine defect in an assembly script and is squarely inside this audit's failure-path scope, so I am not killing it as hypothetical.

STRUCTURAL MECHANISM FULLY VERIFIED AGAINST HA SOURCE; TRIGGER IS A FAULT CONDITION, NOT A USER ACTION.

Verified in HA 2026.5.3: config_entries.py:886-893 — a raise out of async_setup_entry is caught, and the `finally:` block runs only `await self._async_process_on_unload(hass)` (i.e. only entry.async_on_unload callbacks); our async_unload_entry is NOT called. config_entries.py:1007-1010 confirmed verbatim: `if self.state is not ConfigEntryState.LOADED: self.async_cancel_retry_setup(); self._async_set_state(hass, NOT_LOADED); return True` — so a subsequent Reload ALSO skips async_unload_entry. Both HA claims are exactly right.

Verified in-repo: __init__.py:265 is the ONLY entry.async_on_unload in the whole entry setup. battery_manager.start (336), error_tracker.start (344), the four service registrars (390-393) and the eight listener register() calls (398-405) are unguarded, with no try/finally around the assembly. The duplication consequence is real: core/error_tracker.py:218 holds `self._vacuum_unsubs` PER INSTANCE, and :382 `if vacuum_entity_id in self._vacuum_unsubs: return` is a per-instance guard a second instance cannot see. The clobber is real and I confirmed the exact line: core/error_tracker.py:1069-1071 `self._hass.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._hass.async_create_task, self._manager.async_save())` against the OLD manager, and core/manager.py:803-805 `async_save` = `await self.storage.async_save(self.data)` — an unconditional whole-blob write. Same clobber shape as audit #14, reached by a different door.

WHERE I DISAGREE: the proposed triggers are weaker than claimed. I checked each. 'Corrupt storage reaching an unguarded ensure_record' — manager.async_initialize is already wrapped in ConfigEntryNotReady (237-240) and load_stored_adapter_configs (adapters/config_loader.py:36-62) type-checks and try/excepts every row. 'ImportError in a lazily-imported listener module' — listeners/ and services/ are imported at MODULE top level (services/__init__.py:22-35), so an ImportError fails the integration import outright rather than mid-setup. The strongest surviving trigger is line 407 `async_forward_entry_setups` -> `integration.async_get_platforms(platforms)` (config_entries.py:2724-2727), which DOES propagate ImportError if a platform module fails to import (a partial/corrupt HACS deploy) — and by that point every subsystem is live. Note that platform-BODY exceptions do NOT reach it (entity_platform.py:518-525 swallows and returns False), so the window is narrower than implied.

MEDIUM is correct and I leave it: narrow, fault-only trigger, but the outcome when it fires is durable-store clobber.

survived.title: Five learning services registered during setup are missing from async_unregister_learning_services, so they survive unload as ghost services
survived.mechanism: async_setup_entry line 391 awaits async_register_learning_services, which registers 21 services (learning/services.py:735-815). async_unregister_learning_services (901-918), called from async_unload_entry line 490, removes only 16. An AST diff of async_register/async_remove call arguments in that file shows exactly five registered-but-never-removed: SERVICE_SET_LEARNING_PROCESSING, SERVICE_PROCESS_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_CONFIRM_EXTERNAL_RUN, SERVICE_GET_EXTERNAL_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_DISCARD_EXTERNAL_RUN. The unregister function is a hand-maintained flat list of async_remove calls with no shared tuple, unlike services/__init__.py (which walks each submodule's SERVICES tuple), mapping_services.py (ALL_MAPPING_SERVICES) and themes/services.py (inline loop) — all three of which I AST-verified as symmetric.
survived.user_impact: After the integration is unloaded, disabled or deleted, those five eufy_vacuum.* services stay listed and callable in Developer Tools and in automations. Calling one raises an unhandled KeyError from `hass.data[DOMAIN]["runtime"]` (learning/services.py:252-254) instead of HA's clean "service not found", so an automation that touches process_pending_runs or confirm_external_run fails with a traceback rather than a comprehensible error. No data is lost — every one of the five handlers resolves the core manager before doing any work.
survived.guards_checked: async_unload_entry lines 489-493 (the four unregister calls plus battery_rebaseline — no catch-all sweep of DOMAIN services); services/__init__.py:66-71 (walks SERVICES tuples — the pattern this file does not use); the five handlers at learning/services.py:300, 365 and their siblings — each calls _get_core_manager(hass) first, which is what keeps this LOW rather than a data-mutation path; _get_learning_manager (257-263) will lazily re-create hass.data[DOMAIN]["learning"] post-unload, but it is never reached first.
confirmations: CONFIRMED by my own independent AST pass over learning/services.py (I did not take the finder's count on trust): async_register_learning_services issues 21 hass.services.async_register calls; async_unregister_learning_services issues 16 async_remove calls. The set difference is exactly the five named: SERVICE_SET_LEARNING_PROCESSING (registered :773), SERVICE_PROCESS_PENDING_RUNS (:780), SERVICE_CONFIRM_EXTERNAL_RUN (:787), SERVICE_GET_EXTERNAL_PENDING_RUNS (:794), SERVICE_DISCARD_EXTERNAL_RUN (:801). Also confirmed the severity-limiting claim: _get_core_manager (learning/services.py:252-254) is `return hass.data[DOMAIN]['runtime']` — a bare subscript, so confirm/get_external_pending/discard raise KeyError before touching data, while handle_set_learning_processing (:455) and handle_process_pending_runs (:461) use hass.data.get(DOMAIN, {}).get(DATA_RUNTIME) and return {'error':'manager_unavailable'}. No data mutation is reachable post-unload, so LOW is the right call.

CONFIRMED BY MACHINE CHECK. I ran an independent AST diff over learning/services.py: async_register_learning_services registers 21 services, async_unregister_learning_services removes 16, MISSING = exactly {SERVICE_SET_LEARNING_PROCESSING, SERVICE_PROCESS_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_CONFIRM_EXTERNAL_RUN, SERVICE_GET_EXTERNAL_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_DISCARD_EXTERNAL_RUN}, EXTRA = {} — the finder's list is exact.

Handler behaviour verified line by line: _get_core_manager (learning/services.py:252-254) is `return hass.data[DOMAIN]['runtime']` — a bare subscript, no .get. handle_confirm_external_run (:270), handle_get_external_pending_runs (:301) and handle_discard_external_run (:366) each call it first, so post-unload they raise KeyError (on 'runtime', or on DOMAIN itself when __init__.py:545-546 popped the whole dict). handle_set_learning_processing (:455) and handle_process_pending_runs (:461) use `hass.data.get(DOMAIN, {}).get(DATA_RUNTIME)` and return {'error':'manager_unavailable'} — exactly as claimed. The asymmetry-vs-siblings claim also holds: services/__init__.py:66-71 walks each submodule's SERVICES tuple; learning/ has no such tuple and is hand-listed.

Trigger: disable or delete the integration, then call eufy_vacuum.confirm_external_run from Developer Tools or an automation -> raw KeyError traceback instead of 'service not found'. No data touched (every handler resolves the manager before doing work). LOW is the right call and the other two finders over-rated it.

survived.title: Panels registered outside async_setup_entry are never tracked, so unload cannot remove them — and setup then re-adds the "no vacuum configured" fallback panel next to the working one
survived.mechanism: async_unload_entry (line 471) removes ONLY the panel urls recorded in hass.data[DOMAIN][f"_panels_{entry.entry_id}"], and that list is built exclusively inside async_setup_entry (lines 412-450). Two other call sites register per-vacuum panels and append to nothing: setup/workflow.py:106 (add_vacuum — the primary onboarding action, invoked from the card) and services/setup.py:307 (setup_set_panel_title, replace=True). panels.async_register_vacuum_panel swallows the duplicate-url ValueError and returns None (panels.py:89-91), and __init__.py:420 drops a None silently — so a panel that is already registered is never re-recorded either. Concrete sequence, all of it the documented onboarding path (the config flow's vacuum picker is optional; the entry's own default notes string says "Open the Vacuum Agent panel in the sidebar to add your vacuum"): (1) install with a blank CONF_VACUUM_ENTITY_ID -> get_known_vacuum_ids() is empty -> registered_panels == [] -> fallback panel "eufy-vacuum" registered and tracked; (2) user adds the vacuum from that panel -> workflow.add_vacuum registers "eufy-vacuum-<object_id>" and does not track it; (3) any reload (options save, HACS update, homeassistant.reload_config_entry) -> unload pops ["eufy-vacuum"] and removes only the fallback; the per-vacuum panel survives because it was never in the list; (4) setup re-runs, async_register_vacuum_panel hits the still-live duplicate, returns None, registered_panels stays EMPTY, so the `if not registered_panels:` branch at line 428 concludes "no managed vacuums yet" and re-registers the fallback setup-placeholder panel. Steady state after every reload until a full HA restart: a duplicate sidebar entry, one of which renders the "you haven't set up a vacuum yet" placeholder for an install that HAS a managed vacuum. Same untracked panel also survives disabling or deleting the integration entirely (frontend panels live in memory until restart), leaving a sidebar entry whose service calls no longer exist.
survived.user_impact: After adding a vacuum through the panel (the advertised onboarding path), the sidebar shows two "Vacuum Agent" entries and one of them tells the user the integration is not set up yet — with no error or log warning above debug level. Disabling or removing the integration leaves a dead sidebar entry behind until Home Assistant is restarted.
survived.guards_checked: panels.async_register_vacuum_panel — the `except ValueError: return None` at panels.py:89-91 is the swallow, not a rescue; __init__.py:420 `if panel_url:` — this is the drop, not a guard. __init__.py:447 `except ValueError` on the fallback registration only protects the fallback itself. _remove_panel_for_vacuum (line 562) DOES scan every `_panels_*` list, but it is only reached from _teardown_vacuum (device deletion), never from unload, and its scan cannot find a url that was never appended. hass.data pop at line 471 defaults to [] so no KeyError masks it. Checked tests/: grep for `_panels_` across the whole test tree returns nothing — no test covers the tracking list. Full HA restart does mask it (panels are re-registered into a fresh registry and tracked), which is why it reads as intermittent.
survived.area: DOWN — teardown and symmetry (async_unload_entry / async_remove_entry / _teardown_vacuum / _remove_panel_for_vacuum / _schedule_clear_configured_vacuum / async_remove_config_entry_device)
confirmations: CONFIRMED — same defect and same verified chain as A1-UP-1 (duplicate finding; the two finders reached it independently and the mechanisms agree). I re-checked the parts DOWN-1 states differently: __init__.py:471 pops with a [] default so no KeyError masks anything; _remove_panel_for_vacuum (562-573) does scan every _panels_* list, but it is reached only from _teardown_vacuum via async_remove_config_entry_device (device deletion), never from unload, and its scan cannot find a url that was never appended; a full HA restart does mask it because DATA_PANELS is in-memory. One inaccuracy that does not change the verdict: DOWN-1 names services/setup.py:307 (setup_set_panel_title) as a second untracked registrar — it uses replace=True on a url that is already in the tracked list, so it is not a leak site. workflow.py:106 alone is sufficient.

DUPLICATE of A1-UP-1 (same file, same line, same mechanism) — and this write-up states the reproducer MORE accurately: it correctly starts from a blank-vacuum install, which is the only ordering in which the `if not registered_panels:` fallback branch at __init__.py:428 actually fires. I re-derived and confirmed that sequence step by step; see my A1-UP-1 verdict for the full source verification (panels.py:89-91 swallow, HA frontend/__init__.py:386-387 ValueError, panel_custom passing no `update=`, setup/workflow.py:105-110 untracked registration, services/setup.py:161-167 auto-reload).

One correction: the claim that the untracked panel 'also survives disabling or deleting the integration entirely' is true, but async_remove_config_entry_device -> _teardown_vacuum -> _remove_panel_for_vacuum (__init__.py:562-573) DOES remove it by computed url on the device-deletion path — so deleting the DEVICE cleans it up; deleting/disabling the ENTRY does not. Worth keeping straight when fixing.

SEVERITY: not HIGH. Presentation-layer only, no durable data lost, no wrong robot action, fully cleared by an HA restart -> MEDIUM.

survived.title: async_unregister_learning_services removes 16 of the 21 services async_register_learning_services registers — 5 survive unload and 3 raise a bare KeyError when called
survived.mechanism: AST-verified count: async_register_learning_services registers 21 services on LEARNING_DOMAIN (== DOMAIN, learning/services.py:39); async_unregister_learning_services (line 901) hand-lists 16 hass.services.async_remove calls. Missing: set_learning_processing, process_pending_runs, confirm_external_run, get_external_pending_runs, discard_external_run. Unlike every sibling registrar this module has no SERVICES/SERVICE_NAMES tuple to walk (services/__init__.py:71, mapping_services.py:2943 and themes/services.py:332 all iterate a declared tuple and are 12/12, 30/30 and 11/11 symmetric), so the list is hand-maintained and drifted. After async_unload_entry line 490 runs, those 5 remain callable. handle_confirm_external_run (269), handle_get_external_pending_runs (300) and handle_discard_external_run (365) all begin with _get_core_manager(hass) == hass.data[DOMAIN]["runtime"] (line 254, subscript not .get) — DATA_RUNTIME was popped at __init__.py:542, so the call raises an unhandled KeyError out of the service handler. handle_set_learning_processing (454) and handle_process_pending_runs (460) do guard with .get and return {"error": "manager_unavailable"}. A reload masks it (re-registration overwrites); disabling or deleting the entry does not.
survived.user_impact: After disabling or removing the integration, 5 eufy_vacuum services stay listed in Developer Tools and remain selectable in automations/scripts; calling confirm_external_run, get_external_pending_runs or discard_external_run produces a raw KeyError traceback instead of "service not found". The three affected services are the external-run review wizard's backend, so an automation built on them fails obscurely rather than reporting the integration is gone.
survived.guards_checked: services/__init__.py:66-71 (async_unregister_services) only walks the services/ package submodules — it never touches learning/. mapping and themes unregister via their own complete tuples. __init__.py:489-493 calls all four unregister helpers plus battery_rebaseline explicitly, so nothing downstream sweeps the domain. _get_core_manager uses hass.data[DOMAIN]["runtime"] with a subscript — no .get fallback. hass.data[DOMAIN] itself is still present after unload (see DOWN-3), so the failure is a KeyError on "runtime" rather than on DOMAIN either way.

Entity-level subscription lifecycle across a reload — every entity that subscribes in async_added_to_hass unsubscribes in async_will_remove_from_hass (binary_sensor.py:90-99; sensor/lifecycle.py:81-112 covers all four of its unsubs including an async_track_time_interval), and every platform-level manager callback and timer is registered with entry.async_on_unload (button.py:108-113 run-profile callback; switch.py:97-101 and number.py:127-130 room-update callbacks; sensor/__init__.py:346-378 four manager callbacks, :418 the job-finished bus listener, :431 and :471 two async_track_time_interval handles). No unique_id is derived from anything that changes across a reload — they are all f'{vacuum_entity_id.replace(".","_")}_{suffix}' — so entities restore rather than duplicate.

listeners/* register/remove symmetry — all eight modules registered at __init__.py:398-405 are removed at :480-487, remove() pops a private hass.data key holding the unsub list, and register() calls remove() FIRST (verified in listeners/job_progress.py:53-54 and listeners/discovery.py:52-54), so even a double-setup without an intervening unload cannot double-subscribe or orphan a ticker.

hass.data[DOMAIN] key symmetry for keys async_setup_entry writes directly — DATA_ADAPTER_COORDINATOR (:232 / popped :535), DATA_RUNTIME (:316 / :542), DATA_LEARNING (:318 / :543), DATA_BATTERY (:337 / :505), DATA_ERROR_TRACKER (:345 / :511), 'mapping_tracker' (:370 / :502), '_panels_<entry_id>' (:450 / :471). Every one is popped. The only leftover DOMAIN keys come from RELOAD-4.

Subsystem stop() coverage — ErrorTracker.stop (core/error_tracker.py:336-352) tears down per-vacuum state listeners AND cancels every pending grace-window async_call_later; BatteryHealthManager.stop and MappingTracker.unregister_all are both invoked; the AdapterCoordinator shutdown sits in a `finally` (__init__.py:532-540) so it runs even if a per-vacuum unregister_adapter_config raises, which is what keeps the module-level active-coordinator pointer from leaking into the second setup.

Service register/unregister symmetry outside learning/ — verified name-by-name via AST: all 13 modules in services/ have SERVICES tuples that exactly match what their register() calls (including services/debug.py, whose SERVICES aliases debug_capture.SERVICE_NAMES); ALL_MAPPING_SERVICES covers all 30 mapping registrations; the themes unregister tuple covers all 11. Only learning/ is asymmetric (RELOAD-2).

Unload/setup ORDER — unload does platforms first (:467) and only then listeners, services and subsystems, i.e. the exact reverse of setup, so no entity outlives the manager callbacks it is subscribed to. Setup publishes DATA_RUNTIME at :316, well before the forward at :407, so the platforms' bare `hass.data[DOMAIN]['runtime']` subscripts (button.py:28, number.py:33, sensor/__init__.py:85, room_entities.py:61) cannot KeyError on the reload path.

Reload-trigger serialization — all three triggers (the options update listener at __init__.py:265/462, the UI Reload button, and services/setup.py:162-167 which spawns a reload from inside setup_add_vacuum) route through hass.config_entries.async_reload, which holds entry.setup_lock across BOTH the unload and the setup (homeassistant/config_entries.py:2430-2431). Two overlapping reloads therefore serialize; the second async_setup_entry cannot interleave with the first async_unload_entry. Considered and rejected as a finding: services/setup.py:166 and _async_update_listener use async_reload rather than HA's recommended async_schedule_reload, but async_reload itself calls entry.async_cancel_retry_setup() before taking the lock, and the residual setup-retry race requires the entry to be in SETUP_RETRY — in which case _add_vacuum would have returned 'error' (manager is None) and never scheduled the reload at all.

Considered and rejected: the `if unload_ok:` gate at __init__.py:469 skipping ALL cleanup when one platform fails to unload. This is HA's documented idiom; on a False return HA marks the entry FAILED_UNLOAD and refuses to run async_setup_entry (config_entries.py:2431-2432), so the second setup can never observe the half-torn state, and a second Reload re-runs the unload cleanly. Not a finding.

TRAP (a) CHECKED EXPLICITLY, not assumed: for every leak claim I asked whether HA already cleans it up. It does not in any of these cases. Panels live in hass.data[DATA_PANELS] with no entry association and are only removed by an explicit async_remove_panel call. Services are global and only removed by an explicit async_remove. Trap (b) is the operative one throughout: the water-amendment timer, the debug auto-stop timer, and the amendment's state subscription are all bare async_call_later / async_track_state_change_event with unsubs held in closures, never registered with entry.async_on_unload — and entry.async_on_unload appears exactly ONCE in the entire 728-line file, at line 265, for the update listener. That last one matters most: an unconditional reload-on-update listener is the HA-DOCUMENTED idiom, and its only real danger is borrowed from audit #14's uncancelled manager work and from the panel bug. Rating it HIGH double-counts the same damage across three findings. Net after correction: 0 CRITICAL, 0 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 5 LOW across the 8 distinct defects.

ONE FACTUAL CORRECTION worth carrying into any fix. A1-UP-1 claims the duplicate-fallback-panel loop hits "every second and later vacuum unconditionally". It does not. I re-derived both orderings: with vacuum A already tracked and B added via the panel, unload removes A, setup re-registers A, `registered_panels` is non-empty, and the `if not registered_panels:` branch at __init__.py:428 never fires — B is merely untracked (A4-RELOAD-1's exact claim). The duplicate-fallback loop needs ALL known vacuums untracked, i.e. the first vacuum added from a blank install (A2-DOWN-1's ordering, which is correct). The two symptoms are different reproducers of one root cause: `if panel_url:` at :420 silently drops a url that panels.py:89-91 turned into None.

Also note that _remove_panel_for_vacuum (__init__.py:562-573) DOES remove the untracked panel on DEVICE deletion; it is entry unload/disable/delete that cannot.

TWO CROSS-CUTTING ROOT CAUSES, which is where a fix should land rather than on 8 sites:
1. Registration and removal are tracked in DIFFERENT places by DIFFERENT hands. `_panels_<entry_id>` is a ledger only one of three registration call sites writes to; the learning unregister is a hand-copied flat list while all three sibling registrars walk a declared tuple. This is the same "hand-copied literals" shape as the sibling sweep in [[feedback_centralize_question_not_vocabulary]] — the fix is to make registration itself append to the ledger (or return one), not to add a fourth hand-maintained list.
2. `entry.async_on_unload` is used EXACTLY ONCE in the entire entry setup (__init__.py:265, for the update listener). Every other row in the systemic table — the panels, the debug autostop timer, the water-amendment listener and timer, and audit #14's manager work — is unwound (if at all) by hand inside async_unload_entry, which is precisely why the ones registered outside async_setup_entry have no unwind at all. Routing loop-lifetime work through entry.async_on_unload closes the panel gap, the debug-timer gap, the water-amendment gap AND the failure-unwind gap (A1-UP-2) at one seam, because HA runs those callbacks even when setup RAISES — verified at config_entries.py:891-893.

ON A1-UP-2 SPECIFICALLY: I confirmed both HA claims verbatim (setup raise -> only async_on_unload callbacks run, our async_unload_entry never called; later reload returns True early at :1007-1010 because state is not LOADED), and the clobber mechanism it lands on (core/error_tracker.py:1069-1071 firing the OLD manager's async_save, core/manager.py:803-805 writing the whole blob). But I checked its three proposed triggers and two do not hold: storage corruption is already fenced by ConfigEntryNotReady and by type-checked/try-excepted loading in adapters/config_loader.py, and listener/service modules are imported at package top level so an ImportError kills the import, not the setup. The surviving trigger is `async_forward_entry_setups` -> `integration.async_get_platforms` raising ImportError on a partial deploy (platform-BODY exceptions do not reach it — entity_platform.py:518-525 swallows them). Real, but fault-only. Kept at MEDIUM.

CLEAN AREAS the finders recorded that I spot-checked and agree with: the ConfigEntryNotReady path at :237-240 is genuinely harmless on retry; listeners/*.register() are idempotent (each calls remove() first); the try/finally around coordinator shutdown at :517-540 is correct; mapping/themes/services unregister paths are symmetric (my AST diff agrees); _teardown_vacuum's per-vacuum unwind is thorough and each step is isolated; and _schedule_clear_configured_vacuum correctly clears the key from BOTH data and options and correctly defers to avoid racing HA's device removal.

Not verified by me (out of scope, flagged for the parent): there is still no async_migrate_entry, and CONFIG VERSION is 1 with no minor_version — so the storage-schema question the brief raised remains open and unanswered by any of the four finders.
